claim: The approve act tests the same money as the price re-check: ADR 0244 D3, the founder's answer 1 of 2026-09-30, verbatim pick "Both use the larger (Recommended)". procurement.service.ts assertApprovalAllowed (POST orders/:id/approve and its seal mint) reads total_cost, final/negotiated/quoted price and quantity, and tests effectiveTotal: the larger of total_cost and unit price (final ?? negotiated ?? quoted) x quantity, from order-price-recheck.ts, the function the re-check uses. Before, it tested total_cost alone, so an order whose total_cost understated its price x quantity could be sealed by a manager under a ceiling it was over. The /orders readout's walk (approvalGate, walkOrdersUnderTest) tests the same money, so the page's who-may-seal and the act cannot disagree. With no unit price the total alone decides, as before. NOT this claim: the settings register's retrospective (settings/approval-thresholds.service.ts) still counts on total_cost, an open question. Behaviour: order-approval-gate.spec.ts, 2 new REVERT-FAILS cases red on d06aa4de4 (#541's head) and one pinning the no-unit-price case; the two fixtures that priced an order above its own total now state consistent figures; mutations of the act or the page falling back to total_cost are killed in jest, while dropping a column from either read survives jest (the stub ignores select lists) and is caught here. This verify: 7 reasons on d06aa4de4, and 7 of 7 tripwire mutations (the act and the page each falling back to total_cost and each dropping a column from its read, effectiveTotal losing its max, a spec case unmarked, the ADR's built bracket) each reported, 2026-09-30.
